newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian opposition accuses PM of fear campaign.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian opposition accuses PM of fear campaign.

text.p: Opposition leader Sam Rainsy on Tuesday accused Cambodia's second prime minister of political scare tactics, and vowed to form a broad coalition to challenge the co-premier in upcoming elections.

In an interview with Reuters at his Phnom Penh home, Sam Rainsy, who heads the Khmer Nation Party (KNP), said, "(Second Prime Minister) Hun Sen is trying to create an atmosphere of fear and of terror in order to crack down on (political) openings."
He said Hun Sen's announcement on Monday that a large network of Khmer Rouge spies was threatening the country and diplomatic missions was meant to intimidate Cambodians and foreigners.
"These Khmer Rouge are fake Khmer Rouge," Sam Rainsy said in reference to 80 self-proclaimed spies who defected to the government in a ceremony led by Hun Sen on Monday.
Hun Sen had said at the ceremony that the defections should not be interpreted as false or politically motivated.
But Sam Rainsy said, "The (fake Khmer Rouge) are playing comedy at the instruction of Hun Sen himself. This is very Machiavellian."
He vowed to form a broad coalition to challenge Hun Sen's formerly communist Cambodian People's Party (CPP) in national elections scheduled for 1998.
"One day, very soon, hopefully, (and) long before the elections, FUNCINPEC, BLDP, KNP and the other non-communist parties will join together in order to meet the communists (CPP)," he told Reuters.

Sam Rainsy's comments were the strongest sign yet that he would ally with First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party and the minority Buddhist Liberal Democratic Party in a coalition to unite all major parties against the CPP.
Last year, former finance minister Sam Rainsy was expelled from FUNCINPEC and the national assembly for his outspoken views on government corruption and national reform.
In November 1995, he formed the KNP, which has not been officially recognised by the Cambodian government.
But in recent weeks, the frosty relations between Ranariddh and Sam Rainsy have thawed as both sides size up their chances in national elections.
Ranariddh has said FUNCINPEC is ideologically closer to Sam Rainsy than Hun Sen, his partner in Cambodia's uneasy coalition government, and suggested a FUNCINPEC-KNP coalition.
Sam Rainsy seemed to embrace the concept on Tuesday and said he would mobilise overseas Cambodian voters, which he estimated at 200,000, in support of the KNP or the coalition.
He said he would also seek to strengthen a regional network of democratic leaders.

"Some authoritarian leaders in Asia pretend that there is an Asian way toward democracy and development. We don't believe in such a claim at all. We deeply believe that human rights and democracy are universal concepts," he said.
"Dictators in the world tend to stick together.... We wonder why liberal democrats could not help each other too."
Sam Rainsy said he had some concerns about the timing of national elections, which could be delayed by a lack of electoral laws.

"This can lead to two possibilities: either political intimidation will lead to fake elections...or violence and different troubles will be used as a pretext to delay the elections," he said, blaming reported incidents of political intimidation on the CPP.
CPP officials have maintained that their party only wants peace and have accused FUNCINPEC of trying to provoke trouble by bringing false charges of CPP intimidation.
